answer.rationale: Two of the three pressures are funnel-health problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record points twice in the same direction: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable first-week activation lift). Convergent, independently consolidated evidence on the exact metrics that are decaying makes simplify_onboarding the best single-slot bet for sustainable qualified revenue, since it compounds rather than buying volume. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct load-bearing claim for the action I intend and I want to confirm the effect was on completion/adoption itself and not a proxy, and memory_73 because it is the strongest competing option under competitive price pressure but carries an explicit self-flagged defect (cohorts pooled after a mid-test redefinition), which means its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' could be an artifact; if the archive shows the pooling was benign, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender and I would want to know that before spending the slot. I am deliberately not verifying memory_91 or memory_44: activation_messaging treats the symptom downstream of the broken onboarding step, and enterprise_sales_assist addresses a segment that is not the one under attack. Downstream value risk is flagged mainly against the pricing path: discount-led SMB acquisition tends to import price-sensitive accounts with weaker retention and to reset reference prices, so it can raise near-term revenue while lowering the sustainable qualified revenue we are optimizing for; a smaller risk on the onboarding path is that cutting required fields removes qualification signal and degrades lead routing, so the test should hold data-quality and downstream-conversion guardrails, not just completion rate. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, none re-measured on day-76 conditions, and the current declines may share an unobserved common cause (traffic-mix shift from the competitor's launch) that would make any funnel fix look weaker or stronger than it is. Running at standard_experiment scale rather than broad rollout keeps that exposure bounded; if verification undercuts memory_86, I would fall back to activation_messaging at small_guarded_test scale rather than defaulting to price.
